report.summary: Property-based testing (Hypothesis, QuickCheck) can serve as fitness by counting passing properties. Daikon infers invariants from execution traces; measured: ~90% true over test suites (Ernst et al., ICSE 1999). Using inferred invariants as properties for fitness in evolution is underexplored; one study reports 20% improvement in test coverage (uncertain). Actionable: mine invariants with Daikon from passing runs, convert to Hypothesis tests, and use pass rate as fitness signal in multi-objective optimization.
risks: fitness based on property pass rate can be noisy

handoff.suggestion: Start by applying Daikon to your codebase's passing test suite to extract likely invariants. Convert the top-ranked invariants into Hypothesis test functions. Use the number of passing property tests as one component of a multi-objective fitness function, balancing with other signals like static metrics or runtime performance. Validate on a small corpus of programs with known bugs to see if the fitness correlates with correctness.
